articleSummary: Rocky Mountain spotted fever (febre maculosa) in Americana, São Paulo, Brazil continues with three deaths this year. A 49-year-old man, hospitalized in a public hospital, died on July 24; diagnosis was confirmed by Instituto Adolfo Lutz. The probable infection source is under investigation by PVCE. As of August 17, Americana has 34 RMSF notifications, with 22 discarded, nine awaiting results, and three deaths. Since the start of the month, the city has applied Metarhizium fungus to control the star tick (Amblyomma cajennense) in risk areas, including Praia dos Namorados and Avenida Bandeirantes, in partnership with Instituto Biológico and Toyobo, under health authorities. PVCE also installs fences and signs and advises avoiding risk habitats such as river margins, lagoons, and riparian zones. Symptoms include high fever, body and head pains, chills, and a red rash; suspected cases should seek care promptly and report exposure.

articleHeadline: Latest ebola outbreak becomes deadliest in DRC's history
articleSummary: DRC's Ebola outbreak, the deadliest in country’s history, is in an 'intense transmission' phase per WHO. About six months into the outbreak, the DRC National Institute of Public Health reports 2,325 deaths among 4,945 confirmed infections, with 101 new cases in the last 24 hours. The true burden may be higher; Airfinity estimates infections fivefold official counts. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo Ebola, first identified in Uganda in 2007, likely originating in fruit bats and spreading between people through contact with blood and body fluids. Containment is hindered by armed conflict, population displacement, and fragile health systems; many deaths occur in communities, suggesting undetected cases. Uganda reports 20 cases and 2 deaths, with no new cases in over a month. Two Bundibugyo vaccines have begun phase 1 trials (Moderna and Oxford), with Serum Institute manufacturing 620,000 Oxford doses; WHO plans Merck vaccine trial for Zaire strain to assess cross-protection.

articleHeadline: Lightweight non-contrast CT-based multimodal artificial intelligence for subtype classification of hepatic cystic echinococcosis in resource-limited clinical settings - npj Digital Medicine
articleSummary: Hepatic cystic echinococcosis (HCE) subtype classification using lightweight non-contrast CT–based multimodal AI achieved macro-AUCs of 0.942 (internal validation) and 0.931 (external validation) for CE1-CE5 subtyping, in resource-limited settings. A two-stage framework performs automated lesion segmentation followed by CE1-CE5 classification, integrating 2D multi-slice, 3D volumetric, and radiomics features. Development used 733 patients from Qinghai University Affiliated Hospital; external validation included 261 patients from two county-level hospitals. The multimodal model outperformed single-modality counterparts, with most errors between adjacent transitional stages. In a reader study, AI-assisted interpretation yielded higher macro-AUCs than physician-only interpretation in tertiary (0.970 vs. 0.905) and county-level cohorts (0.963 vs. 0.902). Interpretability analyses localized subtype-relevant regions and quantified patient-specific modality contributions, supporting prospective human-in-the-loop evaluation of non-contrast CT–based AI as a decision-support tool in resource-limited clinical settings.

articleHeadline: Brasil registra menor número de casos de malária em quase 50 anos - Metro 1
articleSummary: Brazil reported 118,037 locally transmitted malaria cases in 2025, down 14.8% from 2024, with malaria deaths down 30%. This is the lowest malaria burden in 48 years, the least since 1978; ministry statistics go back to 2007. The decline is linked to tafenoquine, a single-dose antimalarial drug made available by Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS) since 2024 to prevent relapse. Brazil became the first country to provide tafenoquine to children through the public health system, with expectations of further reductions as children—accounting for about half of malaria cases in Brazil—are covered by the program. Authorities continue surveillance in endemic regions and emphasize the policy's impact on pediatric cases and overall transmission.

articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is now the deadliest in the country's history, with 2,325 deaths and 4,945 confirmed cases, including 101 new cases in the past 24 hours. The circulating Bundibugyo species has no approved vaccines or treatments. The case fatality ratio has risen from about 20% in early June to 46%, suggesting late detection rather than increased virulence. Symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and, in severe cases, internal and external bleeding. Transmission is via direct contact with bodily fluids of infected people, living or dead. Global health authorities note only a small number of experimental vaccines/therapies are under evaluation. The outbreak has spread to Uganda earlier, where deaths were limited; that country ended its outbreak last month.

articleSummary: Spain reports 38 Newcastle disease outbreaks in six provinces—Valencia, Valladolid, Zamora, Segovia, Ávila and Salamanca—during the current season that began in late December 2025. The first outbreak was notified on 29 December 2025 at a broiler fattening operation in Llutxent (Valencia). The spread prompted Spain to lose its Newcastle disease-free status with the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH). The loss blocks export-health certificates from CEXGAN, restricting shipments of poultry meat, eggs, live birds, genetic material, day-old chicks, and other avian products. Markets affected include Algeria, Argentina, Bolivia, Ecuador, Venezuela, Bosnia and Herzegovina, China, Colombia, Costa Rica, United Arab Emirates, Hong Kong, Iraq, Japan, Libya, Malaysia, Mexico, Paraguay, Peru, Rwanda, Ukraine, Uruguay and Vietnam. MAPA notes ongoing restrictions tied to a prior 2022 outbreak and ongoing updates as third-country responses evolve.
